fills.researcher_notes: CORRECTS the note in this shard's prior validity entry, which checked only the KHYBER PAKHTOON KHWA section of SNGPL's table. Fetching the raw HTML directly (curl, bypassing the summarizer) shows the SAME named 10in line 'WAH-NOWSHERA(1)' is listed TWICE in this table, once per province the line physically crosses: Sr#175 under PUNJAB, MainLine = 50.41 km (this is the EXACT match to the sheet's current LengthKnown — SNGPL's Punjab-side portion only), and Sr#5 under KHYBER PAKHTOON KHWA, MainLine = 25.13 km (the KP-side portion of the SAME named line, same 10in diameter). SNGPL's province-wise breakup is evidently reporting each cross-provincial line's mileage per province, not as one combined total row. Summed, the full Wah(Punjab)->Nowshera(KP) physical corridor for this 10in line is 50.41 + 25.13 = 75.54 km, which is a close match to the drawn geojson's geodesic 73 km (ratio 73/75.54 = 0.966, inside the 0.75-1.33 tolerance) — far better than the current stated 50.41 km alone (ratio 1.44). This is the exact 'segment of a longer named line' granularity pattern the brief flagged as the working hypothesis for this cluster, confirmed here by SNGPL's own primary source rather than assumed. Tier is medium, not high, because it is a single organization's figures (albeit its own current asset register, summed across two of its own rows for the identically-named line) and because I am proposing a computed sum rather than one single stated total — a human should confirm before pasting whether 75.54 should replace 50.41 outright, or whether GEM prefers to keep this row as the Punjab-only segment (in which case a companion KP-only row/SegmentName note would be the correct fix instead). Not marking UNRESOLVED because there IS a sourced, verified figure that resolves the length_ratio flag far better than the status quo; the remaining open question is which of the two correct framings (single merged row vs Punjab-only + missing KP segment) GEM wants, which is a modeling decision for a human, not a research one.
